summary: Huaiyu Chen specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his master's under Xinjiang Rong at Peking University in 1994 and completed doctoral studies under Stephen F. Teiser (~2000–2005), later serving as assistant professor at Arizona State University (~2006–2012).

Working in Tibetology and religious studies, Huaiyuan Yu earned a Bachelor of Laws from Xiamen University (2015–2019) and an MSc from University College London (2019–2021). As of 2023, Yu is a PhD candidate at Xiamen University.

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. After studying at UCLA (2009–2013), He held postdocs at Oregon Health & Science University and Stanford, served at Sun Yat-sen University (2017–2026), and joined the University of Macau in 2026.
Huawen Bai was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University from ~1951 to ~1955 and subsequently served as a professor there from ~1955 to 1999.

Hubert Decleer was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Étienne Lamotte at KU Leuven in 1975. He held long-term posts at the SIT Graduate Institute, serving as academic director (1987) and senior faculty advisor (1999).

Hubert Durt specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology, studying under Étienne Lamotte (~1959–1968). He served as a professor at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1970–2001), directed the Hobogirin Institute (~1978–2008), and edited Mélanges chinois et bouddhiques (~1978–2018).

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD under Wendy Doniger at the University of Chicago (~1993–1998) and became an associate professor of comparative studies at Ohio State University in ~1998.
Hugh Canning worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his MA at Trinity College, Hartford by 1910, where he was appointed Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology in 1914.

Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist who studied at Keble College, Oxford (~1924–1928). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1947), founded the Tibet Society (1959), and was a visiting professor at the University of Washington (~1961–1962).

Hugh Falconer was a scholar who studied at the University of Aberdeen and earned an MD from Edinburgh (~1826–1829). He served as Superintendent of Saharanpur Botanical Garden (1832) and the Indian Botanic Garden, alongside Calcutta Medical College (1848–1855).

Hugh George Rawlinson was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned an MA at Emmanuel College (~1899–1903). He served as Principal at Karnatak Arts College (1917–1923) and Professor of English Literature at Deccan College (~1919–1933).

Hugh Gray was a scholar of Indology who was educated at Battersea Grammar School. He spent much of his academic career at SOAS and the University of London, where he served as a lecturer from ~1961 to ~1980.

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who earned his doctorate at Stanford University (~1969–1973). He became a professor at Stony Brook University in 1974 and served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (~1976–2013).

Hugh Trevor Lambrick was an Indologist and historian. He earned his BA (~1923–1927) and D.Litt. (1971) at Oxford, served as President of the Sind Historical Society (1940–1943), and became a Fellow and Lecturer at Oriel College.

Hugh van Skyhawk is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer. By 2008, he was Professor of Comparative Religion at Quaid-i-Azam University's Taxila Institute of Asian Civilizations.

Hugo David is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (by 2012) and studied under several traditional teachers. In 2015, he became a permanent member of the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Hugo Ehrlich was a linguist who earned his PhD under Karl Brugmann at the University of Leipzig (~1897–1901) after studying at Jena. In 1912, he was appointed Privatdozent for Indo-European linguistics at the University of Königsberg.
Hugo Enomiya-Lassalle was a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied under traditional teacher Koun Yamada (~1968–1978) and held a post at Sophia University.

Hugo Heinrich Figulla specialized in linguistics and Indology, earning a PhD under Bruno Meissner at Breslau (~1907–1911). He worked at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1934–1936) and served as a Keeper at the British Museum (1946–1963).

Hugo Schuchardt was a linguist who earned his PhD under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl at Bonn (~1861–1864) and studied under August Schleicher. He served as professor of Romance philology at Halle (1873) and Graz (1876–1900).
